out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food items for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: THREE DIFFERENT BIRYANIS ON COUNTER-TOP OBSERVED ON TIME WITHOUT A LABEL.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. PIC ADDED LABEL DURING INSPECTION. PIC UNDERSTANDS FOOD ON TIME SHOULD ALWAYS HAVE A FOUR HOUR TIME LABEL AND THEN DISCARDED OF AFTER THE FOUR HOURS. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED VARIOUS FOOD ITEMS COOLING ON COUNTER- TOP/SHELVES/GRILL-LINE FOR EXTENDED PERIODS OF TIME; OBSERVED COOLING FOODS STORED IN LARGE PORTIONS WITH LIDS.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION ON PROPER COOLING METHODS PROVIDED AGAIN. PLEASE ENSURE COOLING FOODS MEET PROPER COOLING PARAMETERS AND DISCONTINUE LEAVING FOODS OUT ON COUNTER-TOPS FOR EXTENDED PERIODS OF TIMES. COOLING FOODS SHOULD BE STORED IN SMALLER/SHALLOWER PORTIONS AND SHOULD BE PUT IN REFRIGERATION/FREEZERS AS SOON AS POSSIBLE. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BY TIME OF FOLLOW-UP.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: OBSERVED THAWING RAW GOAT SITTING ON COUNTER-TOP AT 39F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PROPER THAWING METHODS WERE DISCUSSED WITH THE PIC. PLEASE ENSURE THAWING FOODS ARE EITHER PUT UNDER CONTINUOUS RUNNING WATER, COOKED FROM FROZEN, OR PUT UNDER REFRIGERATION TO THAW. PIC MOVED RAW GOAT TO A COOLER.
